transcript: After years of it being recommended to me, I finally went to go see sleep no more in New York before it closes now at the end of March. Sleep no more is an immersive adaptation of Macbeth that is told entirely through dance and movement. There is no dialogue in this, which I did not realize going into it. It's a sandbox Immerso show, so essentially you as an audience member have free rein of where you wanna go and how you wanna experience it. Everyone is given a mask that they must wear at all times and told basic rules like you can't talk, you can't touch anybody, actors won't touch you, etc. Etc. And then essentially you get to go into the space and have free rein to go wherever you wanna go. Stage is essentially five different floors, though I hear there's a sixth secret floor that they use for one on one, but I don't know. I did not get taken on the one on one, but as an audience member, you can go anywhere you want in those five floors whenever you want. Can follow a specific actor, you can go off on your own if you want. You can just stay in one room the whole night if that's really what you desire. Actors go through essentially the cycle of the show three times during the night, though you probably won't get in there until either halfway or near the end of the first Cycle, if not later. Now, I went into this completely blind. I did not have a game plan going in. All that I was told is that there's a really cool scene on the fourth floor if you hear techno music, to follow it. So I did that. I saw that scene. I wish I'd done a little bit more research. I liked being able to just go where my instincts told me, but I ended up missing vital scenes that, like, every character was in for some reason, because I didn't want to just follow one person. And so my recommendation for somebody going for the first time during these last two months is to at least one cycle, follow a character so that you see at least the main scenes. I knew I was going to end up missing things in this because of the nature of it, but I didn't think I was gonna miss, like, you know, major. Every character is in the same room at the same time, and I'm off wandering by myself in some weird location. Also knew it was the story of Macbeth, but my perception of where we were in the story at any given time was a little bit off, and so I wasn't quite getting the full story. And then I went back to where I was staying and, like, read through the entire plot and was like, oh, oh, I was so. I was so far off. But Telling this story entirely through dance and movement, I thought, was really, really compelling. At times, though, there were moments where I found myself disengaging or getting a little bit bored. Um, because there was so much else that I knew was happening that, like, I wanted to go explore something else. And so sometimes I just didn't wanna stay and watch somebody do, like, the same movement over and over again when I was like, well, what if there's something more interesting happening? Thing I also found frustrating is sometimes I would go into a room and it would just be so crowded that I couldn't see what was happening. In fact, the best scenes that I found, I found accidentally, because they came to me in rooms that I was already in. I've also been asked by multiple people if it's scary at all, and I would say that it's not. There are moments of Gore, for sure. Um, but if you follow the actors, there's nothing like, there's no. Nobody pops out at you. Um, they sometimes run into a room that you're in, but there's no like. Like, they're not trying to scare you at all. I would say, personally, the scariest thing for me was just being by myself in some of the scenes, because they are, like, there's a creepy aesthetic to them. And so being in that alone definitely felt scary. But if you follow the actors the whole time, it's not scary. At all. I thought it was a cool and unique experience that I didn't really want to do again after I was done with it. But now reading up on it, I'm like, oh, I kind of do want to do that again, but it's, like, so crazy expensive, y'all. I paid full price for this was $150. And every single extension that they've done, it's just got up in price. There is a lottery on today. Ticks that people have been winning. It is possible to win, and even the lottery tickets are $99.
